way Company to Manchoukuo from eleven cities and sixty-two towns and

Manchoukuo, either directly or indirectly. Among them may be mentioned

Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research
Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army.
These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities
in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to
the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With
them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employ-
ment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.
Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo
and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of
all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations,
that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with
an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And
the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's
trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all
phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.

Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company. The last figure included

Of the above mass transfer of personnel, the largest number naturally
came from the South Manchuria Railway Company. On November 30, 1937,
therefore, solemn ceremonies were held at Dairen and all other centers where
the S. M. R. Local Administration Offices are located to bid an official farewell
to the departing employees of the Company. And following this, the Local
Administration Bureau of the South Manchuria Railway Company, with its
thirty-year history of brilliant pioneership and achievement, had been dissolved.
The negotiations over various institutions which the South Manchuria Rail-
way Company has maintained for experimental purposes, which were to be
retained by the Company for the time being, had progressed smoothly after
the above great transfer and a perfect understanding was reached between the
South Manchuria Railway Company and the Manchoukuo Government by March,
1938. As a result, the second great transfer was made on April 1, 1938.
It involved the following institutions : (1) the Kungchuling Agricultural
Experimental Station ; (2) the Hsiungyaocheng Agricultural Experimental
Station ; (3) the Yamuingtzü Agricultural Experimental Station ; (4) the
Liaoyang Cotton Experimental Station ; (5) the Fenghuangcheng Tobacco
Experimental Station ; (6) the Taonan Agricultural Experimental Station ;
(7) the Linhsi Sheep Breeding Farm ; (8) the Kungchuling Sheep Breeding
Farm ; (9) the Veterinary Institute ; (10) the Geological Research Institute ;
(11) the Tumenling Forestry Experimental Station ; and (12) the Hsingcheng
Horticultural Experimental Station. With the above, the Health Research
Institute was transfered to the Kwantung Bureau and the Kwantung Army.
These institutions which served as the basis of various industrial activities
in the past were evaluated at 3,637,000 yen but were to be "loaned" to
the authorities mentioned without compensation for the time being. With
them, an additional number of 445 S. M. R. employees passed into the employ-
ment of Manchoukuo or the Kwantung Bureau.
Thus passed into history Japan's extraterritorial rights in Manchoukuo
and her administrative rights over the S. M. R. Zone. It is to the credit of
all parties concerned, their spirit of cooperation and careful preparations,
that such an epochal transition of first magnitude was consummated with
an amazing smoothness, even without a slightest hitch or difficulty. And
the satisfactory result of the procedure has strongly underwritten Japan's
trust placed upon Manchoukuo, as well as a phenomenal progress made in all
phases of Manchoukuo's statehood during its short span of six years.
